To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the separation level of grades on a multiple-choice test is a function of the number of questions, the proportion of the subject matter known by students, and the grades.

the exact distribution of W is binomial with parameters p and N, and that the separation level S(Z 1, Z2), based on the binomial distribution, is smaller than the separation level based on the normal distribution, for all values of the separation parameter Z.

the separation level of grades on a multiple-choice exam is the same whether the distribution is approximated by the normal distribution or is binomial, and that the separation level can be computed accurately on a programmable calculator using a simple closed-form expression.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the conditional distribution of W is binomial, not normal.
the conditional probability function is not symmetric about the mean, as was assumed by Krutchkoffs, and that the separation level is not symmetric about its mean, either.
the separation level is not a monotonic function of Z1, Z2.
